summary: Split-rate allocation and erroneous prorated credits after mid-cycle plan change
description:
Issue summary: Customer BrightAnswers reports unexpected invoice credits and a missing charge line after they changed from Dedicated Standard to Dedicated Hourly mid-billing-cycle. The charge appears split across two rate tiers and several reserved-hour credits were applied incorrectly, leading to an over-credit on their monthly bill.

Impact: Customer saw a $9,800 credit applied and a missing reserved-hours charge on the invoice for the period 2026-02-15 to 2026-03-15. This affects accounting reconciliation and their internal spend forecasts. The customer is on Dedicated capacity (us-east-1) with sustained hourly reserved capacity and occasional burst usage.

Initial hypothesis: Billing-run proration logic that reconciles reserved-hour commitments and hourly metering likely double-counted overlapping windows after the plan-change event. There may be a race between the plan-change webhook and the hourly postback processing that caused a split allocation: some hours were billed at the old (reserved) rate and others were flagged as hourly and then credited retroactively.

Customer note: They changed plan at 2026-02-20T03:14:22Z (UTC) and immediately ran a multi-region batch job (scheduled at 03:30 UTC) that hit dedicated burst capacity. They attached the invoice PDF and org usage snapshot in the ticket.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer has reserved Dedicated Standard plan (monthly commit) in us-east-1.
2) Submit plan-change request via Console/API to switch to Dedicated Hourly at 2026-02-20T03:14:22Z.
3) Trigger a scheduled burst batch job at 2026-02-20T03:30:00Z.
4) Billing-run processes hourly postbacks and plan-change webhook in the same billing window.
5) Observe invoice rendered for billing period with split line items and retroactive credits.
logs:
Billing-run logs (billing-runner-2026-02-20.log) show plan-change webhook received: event_id=evt_pw_9821 ts=2026-02-20T03:14:22Z.
Hourly-postback: postback_id=pb_88432 ts=2026-02-20T03:33:01Z reports 720 reserved-minutes and 120 burst-minutes.
Credit-applier: txn_id=tx_99102 applied_credit amount=9800 reason=retro-proration scope=org:brightanswers.
Sample trace links: https://logs.redwood.ai/trace/billing/evt_pw_9821, https://logs.redwood.ai/trace/billing/pb_88432.
Stack trace snippet: billing-runner:proration: allocate_range() shows attempted split of window [2026-02-20T03:00:00Z,2026-02-20T04:00:00Z] into two allocations but only persisted one ledger entry for reserved-hours and one credit entry for hourly-hours (missing reconciliation step).
investigation:
Timeline established: webhook arrives at 03:14Z, postback processed at 03:33Z. Billing-run uses in-memory policy cache that had stale plan-mapping for the org for ~12s due to eventual consistency with policy-store.
Reproduction on staging: Simulated plan-change + postback produced identical split-line behavior when plan-change commit and postback landed in different orders. Root cause narrowed to race condition in billing-runner: when an org-level plan update and an hourly postback overlap in the same billable window, the allocation algorithm attempts to split hours but fails to atomically persist both the charge and corresponding offset entries. The offset (credit) path is eventually triggered by the proration reconciler but uses a separate idempotency key causing double-credit when reconciliation runs twice.
Related findings: A prior fix for late postbacks (PR #367) introduced a secondary reconciliation pass which did not respect the newer idempotency schema. See github PRs linked above.
Impact estimate: ~3 customers in dedicated tier in us-east encountered this pattern in the same window; BrightAnswers is the largest affected and is showing a $9.8k over-credit. Total potential exposure ~ $28k across orgs for the affected window.

2026-03-10 13:22 - Linh Tran (Billing Eng): Reproduced on staging with race ordering. Root cause likely in billing-runner allocation code. Assigned fix owner. Linking to PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing-run/pull/479

2026-03-11 17:12 - SRE (ops): Deployed hotfix to billing-runner (canary) that adds atomic write for allocation+offset with new idempotency key. Monitoring for misapplied credits starting 2026-03-12 00:00Z.
2026-03-12 08:00 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer confirmed provisional credit visible; asked for ETA on permanent fix and backfill of other affected customers.
resolution:
Workaround: provisional credit applied to BrightAnswers billing account (ticket note added and customer notified).
Fix deployed: canary hotfix merged (PR #479) and rolled to prod billing-runner: added atomic ledger write and revised idempotency schema for proration reconciler.
Backfill plan: run reconciliation backfill for 2026-02-20 window to detect and re-apply missing/misapplied entries. Backfill job: billing-backfill/2026-02-20-proration-run scheduled 2026-03-13.
Follow-ups: (1) Add unit + integration tests to cover plan-change + postback race, (2) Expand monitoring for credit-applier error rates and idempotency conflict counts, (3) Postmortem to be authored in Confluence and link to this ticket.
Customer communication: Support notified customer of provisional credit and expected restatement by 2026-03-16. Refund/adjustment TL;DR recorded in account notes.
